sections.sectionTitle: Paper 3: Elements of Practical and Physical Geography

topics.title: Map Work, Elementary Surveying, GIS, Statistical Diagrams, Earth Systems, Geomorphology, Weather/Climate, Vegetation, Soils, and Environmental Issues

subtopics.content: Contour map reading, scale, gradients, profiles, drainage patterns, surveying instruments, GIS components/uses, statistical charts, planetary earth, rocks, tectonic/denudational landforms, weather instruments, Koppen climate classification, climate change, vegetation types, soil profile/conservation, environmental resources and hazards
subtopics.objective: Read and interpret contoured survey maps, calculate scales, gradients, and profiles; understand elementary chain/compass surveying; master GIS concepts, data sources, and applications; construct statistical maps and diagrams; explain earth structure, rotation/revolution, ocean currents, and salinity; classify rocks and tectonic landforms (mountains, karsts, coasts); analyze weathering, mass movement, wind/water erosion; use weather instruments and interpret climatic charts/data; analyze climate change, world vegetation types, soil profile formation, soil erosion, and environmental conservation.

sections.sectionTitle: Paper 2: Economic, Human, Regional Geography and Field Work

subtopics.content: World population growth/distribution, rural/urban settlements, migration, transport modes, industrial classification/location, trade, and tourism
subtopics.objective: Analyze world population patterns, growth rates, and migration; distinguish settlement types, functions, and rural-urban interactions; evaluate transport modes and economic development impacts; classify industries and factors affecting location; examine national/international trade and tourism.

regionalGeography.country: Regional Geography of Home Country (e.g. Nigeria / Ghana / Sierra Leone / Liberia / Senegambia)
regionalGeography.content: Physical setting, population, primary activities (agriculture, mining, fishing, lumbering), manufacturing, energy, transport, trade, tourism, environmental development issues, and regional integration (ECOWAS)
regionalGeography.objective: Demonstrate comprehensive knowledge of home country's broad outline, physical relief, climate, population distribution, agricultural systems, mineral/power resources, transport networks, industrial zones, trade, tourism, and development/environmental concerns.

regionalGeography.content: African physical features, minerals, irrigation agriculture (Nile/Niger), plantation farming, oil production, lumbering, gold/copper mining, population distribution, and ECOWAS
regionalGeography.objective: Analyze Africa's broad physical outline, climate, and mineral distribution; detail selected case studies: Nile/Niger irrigation, West/East Africa plantations, Nigeria/Ghana/Libya oil, Equatorial lumbering, South Africa gold mining, Zambia/Zaire copper mining, and ECOWAS objectives.

fieldWork.content: Practical field studies on land use, market surveys, traffic flow, journey to work, and local erosion rates
fieldWork.objective: Execute practical fieldwork observation, data collection, and analysis on local land use, commercial market trends, traffic flow, commuting patterns, or soil erosion.
